method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer); three regulative rules (s 145BA(2) 30-day outcome notice, s 161 28-day appeal, s 158A(2)(a) 28-day point of law appeal) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Health Practitioner Regulation (Adoption of National Law) Act 2009 No 86 (NSW), with Schedule 1 (the NSW modifications of the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law), corpus document nsw_legislation:2024-07-01/act-2009-086 from the Open Australian Legal Corpus (collected 10 March 2025; unofficial, possibly out of date), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-2009-086.txt (text sha256 e7d75b203d5d01fffad69032b8dc870c69282c141bafcefe44162c39cb67f472 per the meta file)

the registered health practitioner the complaint is about (hpr-seat-practitioner.l4)

checks.result: 215 assertions written, 215 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text. hpr-cases-practitioner.l4 includes mirror cases asking the same facts from both seats.
